newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols hold steady ahead of data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols hold steady ahead of data.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options held steady, despite narrow range-trading in the underlying bond market, ahead of Tuesday's June U.S. retail sales data, dealers said.
Activity was very slow, and the soon-expiring August T-bond futures options on the Chicago Board of Trade were fighting an uphill battle against time-decay pressure.
"It's actually quite surprising," said a bank affiliate trader at the CBOT, referring to the resilience in August implied volatility. August options expire on Friday.
He said Tuesday's retail sales and Wednesday's June consumer price index were apparently underpinning volatilities for now.
Shorter-dated options have higher gamma, which provides them quicker premium acceleration but also makes them vulnerable to time decay.
Implied volatility for September and December T-bond futures options were marginally firmer at about 8.2 and 8.5 percent, while August was hovered at just above seven percent.
Still, traders noted that the resilience in the August options was limited to the at-the-money 114 strike price.

As expiration gets closer and volatility levels soften, deltas for out-of-the-money contracts shrink rapidly, making the options deeper out-of-the-money. For instance, the 115 call, only one strike price out from September futures' current level around 114, had a very low delta of only 17.
At the shorter end of the yield curve, Eurodollar volatilities were narrowly mixed as futures continued hovering in narrow ranges.
"They're so low that they're having a hard time going lower going into the numbers," said a brokerage trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
Retail sales data were the only major event foreseeable this week, he said.

"After retail sales, I don't think people much care about CPI (Wednesday's consumer price index), given the PPI numbers that we saw," he said. "By that time, we'll start focussing in on Humphrey-Hawkins."
Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins tesimony is due on July 22.
Trading was light and large-lot deals were scarce in the CME Eurodollar pit. One Wall Street firm was seen buying 1,500 contracts of December 93.75 puts.
Implied volatility for December Eurodollar futures options was off 0.1 point at 9.3 percent, while the March volatility rose 0.1 point to 11.0 percent.
